<blog>

# JMI School Website — Comprehensive Project Analysis

## 1. Project Introduction

**Purpose Statement:**  
JMI School Website is a Next.js-based marketing and examination portal for Jeshurun Montessori International School (JMIS). It serves two primary audiences: parents/guardians seeking school information and students taking computer-based tests (CBT).

**Core Goals and Objectives:**
- Provide a modern, responsive school website with dynamic content managed through an admin dashboard
- Enable students to take objective, completion, and essay-type exams online
- Support admissions inquiries and contact form submissions via email notifications
- Integrate with Supabase for data storage and file management

**Target Audience:**
- Parents and guardians exploring school programs
- Students taking practice exams and assessments
- School administrators managing content and student records

## 2. Technical Architecture

The project follows a modern Next.js App Router architecture with clear separation between marketing pages and exam functionality.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Next.js App] --> B[Marketing Pages]
    A --> C[Exam Portal]
    A --> D[API Routes]
    
    B --> E[Supabase Client]
    C --> F[Exam Components]
    D --> G[Email Service]
    
    E --> H[(Supabase Database)]
    I[Admin Dashboard] --> H
    
    F --> J[Quiz Component]
    F --> K[Completion Exam]
    F --> L[Essay Exam]
```

### Component Breakdown

**Marketing Layer:**
- Home page composed of reusable sections (Hero, Programs, About, Facilities, Gallery, Testimonials, News, FAQ)
- All content dynamically loaded from `jmis_settings` table
- Responsive design using Tailwind CSS and Bootstrap

**Exam System:**
- Multi-session type support (objective, completion, essay)
- Student authentication via database lookup
- Real-time progress tracking and scoring

**Data Flow:**
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client Browser] --> B[React Components]
    B --> C[Supabase Client]
    C --> D[(Supabase Database)]
    B --> E[API Routes]
    E --> F[Email Service]
    F --> G[Gmail SMTP]
```

### Design Patterns

- **Component Composition:** Reusable UI components for consistent branding
- **Hook-based State Management:** Custom hooks for settings and data fetching
- **Server/Client Separation:** Clear distinction between server components and client components
- **Environment Configuration:** Centralized environment variables for external services

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points

**Application Root:**
- `app/layout.jsx` - Global layout with Navbar and Footer
- `app/page.jsx` - Marketing home page composition

**Exam Portal:**
- `app/exam/page.jsx` - Server-side routing wrapper
- `app/exam/ExamClient.jsx` - Dynamic exam component loader

### Core Modules

**Data Access Layer:**
- `lib/supabaseClient.js` - Supabase client configuration
- `lib/useSettings.js` - Shared settings hook for all marketing components
- `lib/enquiry.js` - Contact form handling utilities

**Email Notification System:**
- `app/api/notify/route.js` - Server-side email API endpoint
- `src/api/emailNotificationService.js` - Email service abstraction layer

### Configuration Approach

**Environment Variables:**
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` - Supabase project URL
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` - Public Supabase key
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDENT_PORTAL_URL` - External student portal link
- `GMAIL_USER` & `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` - Email service credentials

**Build Configuration:**
- `next.config.mjs` - Next.js configuration with image optimization
- `postcss.config.mjs` - PostCSS processing setup

### External Dependencies

**Core Framework:**
- Next.js 16.1.0 with React 19.2.3
- Supabase JavaScript client for database operations

**UI Libraries:**
- Bootstrap 5.3.8 for exam interface styling
- React Bootstrap for modal and form components
- React Icons for iconography
- React Toastify for user feedback

**Utilities:**
- Nodemailer for email delivery
- Compromise for natural language processing in essay scoring

### Integration Points

**Supabase Integration:**
- Database tables: `jmis_settings`, `jmis_student`, `jmis_cbtQuestions`, `jmis_cbt_completion`, `jmis_cbt_essay`
- Storage buckets for images and documents
- Real-time capabilities for live updates

**Email Service Integration:**
- Gmail SMTP configuration
- Dynamic recipient resolution from settings
- Error handling and logging

### Component Relationships

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Home Page] --> B[Hero Component]
    A --> C[Programs Component]
    A --> D[About Component]
    A --> E[Facilities Component]
    A --> F[Gallery Component]
    A --> G[Testimonials Component]
    A --> H[News Component]
    A --> I[Faq Component]
    
    B --> J[useSettings Hook]
    C --> J
    D --> J
    E --> J
    F --> J
    G --> J
    H --> J
    I --> J
    
    K[Navbar] --> L[Portal Dropdown]
    L --> M[CBT Portal Link]
    L --> N[Student Portal Link]
    L --> O[Staff Portal Link]
```

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Marketing Website:**
- Dynamic hero carousel with auto-rotation
- Responsive navigation with mobile menu
- Content sections powered by centralized settings
- Contact form with email notifications
- Image gallery with lazy loading

**Computer-Based Testing (CBT):**
- Three exam types: Objective (multiple choice), Completion (fill-in-blank), Essay (free text)
- Student profile verification against database
- Timed exam sessions with progress tracking
- Automatic scoring for objective questions
- Manual grading interface for essays

### Implementation Highlights

**Dynamic Content Management:**
- `components/Hero.jsx` - Auto-rotating carousel with configurable slides
- `lib/useSettings.js` - Centralized settings retrieval hook
- All marketing sections read from single `jmis_settings` row

**Exam System Architecture:**
- `src/pages_components/QuizHome.jsx` - Main exam selection interface
- `app/exam/ExamClient.jsx` - Dynamic exam component router
- Separate components for each exam type with specialized logic

**Email Notification Pipeline:**
- `app/api/notify/route.js` - Secure server-side email sending
- `src/api/emailNotificationService.js` - Abstraction layer for email operations
- Configurable recipients with deduplication logic

### Feature Architecture

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Landing
    Landing --> HeroCarousel: Load Settings
    HeroCarousel --> ProgramSelection: User Interaction
    ProgramSelection --> ExamTypeSelection: Select Subject
    ExamTypeSelection --> ObjectiveExam: Multiple Choice
    ExamTypeSelection --> CompletionExam: Fill-in-Blank
    ExamTypeSelection --> EssayExam: Free Text
    
    ObjectiveExam --> Scoring: Submit Answers
    CompletionExam --> ManualGrading: Submit Answers
    EssayExam --> ManualGrading: Submit Answers
    
    Scoring --> Results: Calculate Score
    ManualGrading --> Results: Teacher Review
    
    Results --> [*]: Complete
```

## 5. Conclusion and Recommendations

### Project Architecture Summary

The JMI School Website demonstrates a well-structured Next.js application that effectively separates concerns between marketing content and functional features. The architecture leverages modern React patterns, Supabase for backend services, and maintains clean separation between server and client components.

**Key Architectural Strengths:**
- Clear separation between marketing pages and exam functionality
- Centralized data management through Supabase
- Reusable component architecture for marketing sections
- Secure email handling through server-side API routes
- Environment-based configuration for different deployment targets

**Potential Improvement Areas:**
- Consider implementing proper error boundaries for better error handling
- Add comprehensive unit testing for critical exam functionality
- Implement caching strategies for frequently accessed settings data
- Consider adding accessibility improvements across all components
- Implement proper rate limiting on email API endpoints

### Actionable Recommendations

1. **Code Organization:** Move shared exam logic into custom hooks or utility functions to reduce duplication
2. **Performance:** Implement React Query or SWR for better data fetching and caching
3. **Security:** Add input validation and sanitization for all user inputs
4. **Testing:** Add comprehensive test coverage for exam scoring algorithms
5. **Monitoring:** Implement error tracking and performance monitoring

### Next Steps for Project Evolution

1. **Enhanced Analytics:** Add analytics tracking for user engagement and exam completion rates
2. **Mobile Optimization:** Further optimize mobile experience for exam taking
3. **Advanced Features:** Implement question randomization and adaptive testing
4. **Integration:** Connect with existing school management systems
5. **Scalability:** Prepare for increased concurrent exam users during peak periods

---

**Sources:**
- [package.json](package.json)
- [next.config.mjs](next.config.mjs)
- [app/layout.jsx](app/layout.jsx)
- [app/page.jsx](app/page.jsx)
- [lib/supabaseClient.js](lib/supabaseClient.js)
- [lib/useSettings.js](lib/useSettings.js)
- [components/Hero.jsx](components/Hero.jsx)
- [app/api/notify/route.js](app/api/notify/route.js)
- [src/api/emailNotificationService.js](src/api/emailNotificationService.js)
- [src/pages_components/QuizHome.jsx](src/pages_components/QuizHome.jsx)
- [app/exam/page.jsx](app/exam/page.jsx)
- [app/exam/ExamClient.jsx](app/exam/ExamClient.jsx)
- [components/Navbar.jsx](components/Navbar.jsx)

</blog>
